What if every AI-generated document carried proof of where it came from?

That is now reality for Claude. Anthropic has launched invisible watermarking across all Claude-generated text — including API and Claude Code outputs. The watermark persists even after the text is copied and pasted elsewhere.

This matters more than it might seem at first glance. Until now, determining whether content was AI-generated relied on imperfect detection tools or self-reporting policies. Both are fragile at scale. Watermarking flips the model — provenance is embedded in the content itself, not dependent on the process that created it.

For enterprises in regulated sectors, this is a governance milestone. Audit trails become more defensible. IP management gets cleaner. Compliance teams gain a tool that works regardless of how many hands the content passes through.

The broader signal is that content provenance is becoming a competitive differentiator in enterprise AI. Procurement teams will start asking every model provider: can you prove where this output came from?
